title: An Introduction to Cybernetics
paper_title: Only variety can absorb variety: how many kinds of trouble can an AI system answer?
paper_frame: Ashby's law of requisite variety says a regulator can only hold outcomes steady if it has at least as many distinct responses as the environment has distinct disturbances. We read the law as a staffing and coverage question for an autonomous system: does every function have a manager that owns code, a clock, a probe and a settler?
data: Theory, with worked examples. The law of requisite variety is the subject of the book's chapter on regulation in the face of disturbance.
summary: Variety is the number of distinguishable states. To keep an essential variable steady, the regulator's variety of responses must match the variety of disturbances; control cannot be bought with less. For software, the variety of responses is the number of distinct, owned ways the system can detect and fix a kind of trouble.
limits: Reading. The source was not machine-read for this paper: its argument is stated in our own words from the publication's well-known content, with no quotation, and a reader should check the claim against the source linked above.
Counting. Variety here is counted as declared roles and loops, which is a lower bound: two managers can respond in the same way. The share measures coverage, not distinctness.
Disturbances. Whether the set of roles matches the set of disturbances the system meets is read from the work queue by a separate reading in the Worker; this paper does not measure it.

misperception.belief: One general-purpose AI agent, given enough instructions, can run a whole organization of work.
misperception.short: One general agent can run everything.
misperception.counter: Control needs as many distinct responses as there are distinct kinds of trouble. A system with one undifferentiated responder fails the law however capable the responder is; owned, distinct managers are the response variety.

findings.claim: Each function the system has to regulate needs a manager that runs named code, keeps a clock, has a closing probe and names the code that settles what it files. A role missing any of these is a response the system cannot actually give.

mechanisms.how: every role names code, clocks, a closing probe and a settler
the check fails a role with no loop, code, clock, probe or settler

findings.claim: Variety of response is useful only if the system can add or change a response when the old ones fail. The second loop must be able to change a parameter of the first loop for each essential variable.

mechanisms.how: each essential variable declares the parameters its second loop may change
step functions are read for every variable

findings.claim: A disturbance the system has no record of has no response. Failure modes that no detector watches are the unmodelled part of the environment.
